_documentation: Single source of truth for the public calendar feeds AND the home-page event cards (#249). Two consumers: (a) `scripts/build-calendar.py` generates `calendar.ics` + `calendar/<slug>.ics` from the top-level scheduling fields (`uid`, `summary`, `description`, `start`, `end`, `location`, `url`, `organizer`, `categories`, `status`); see `docs/architecture.md` *Adding a new event*. (c) `scripts/inject-seo.py` generates each event page's schema.org `Event` node and the `ItemList` on events.html from the same fields, resolving the start and end against `tzid` so the UTC offset is computed rather than typed (#1768); an optional `jsonld` object on an event is merged into the generated node for anything the calendar record has no field for, such as a co-organiser or an attendance mode. (b) The inline JS renderer in `index.html` (+ FR + DE) reads the *renderer* fields (`eventType`, `featured`, `displayDate`, `i18n`, `meta`, `cta`) to build the event cards on the home page. EN content comes from the canonical top-level `summary` + `description` (also used by the .ics); FR + DE overrides live under `i18n.{fr,de}`. The renderer falls back to EN if a locale block is missing, and the hand-coded HTML in each home page is preserved as a `<noscript>`-style fail-soft fallback that the renderer empties on success. When you edit an event here: bump `dtstamp`, run `python3 scripts/build-calendar.py`, and confirm the FR/DE i18n blocks track any EN copy changes. CI runs the drift checker on every PR. Two Indico-derived markers (set by scripts/sync-indico.py, see docs/indico-sync.md): `coHost` is 'joint' for jointly-run EISS × NetSec events (the renderer shows a 'Joint EISS × NetSec' pill) and 'standalone' / absent otherwise; `autoDiscovered: true` flags an entry the sync appended from NetSec's Indico category (#8) carrying only EN copy, to be hand-enriched (richer description, FR/DE) by the maintainer. (c) A third consumer, `assets/js/working-groups.js`, builds the *Related events* cards in each Working Group section from `workingGroups`, `eventType`, `cardTitle`, the optional `cardSubtitle` (a themed strand title, e.g. the policy workshop's), `cardLocation` (a short city-level place, or a localised 'venue to be confirmed' line), `displayDate` and `cta`. Cards run earliest-first, ordered on `start`.

events.description:
Three days of training and mentoring for early-career researchers in European security: research presentations, individualised feedback from senior scholars, and structured mentorship. Open to PhD candidates and post-docs (within one year of defence) in strategic studies and international security, as well as SWAMOS / Euro-SWAMOS alumni.

Scientific Coordinators: Dr Silvia D'Amato, Prof Chiara Ruffa.

Full details: https://netsec-cost.eu/summer-school.html

cardDescription.en: Three days of training and mentoring for early-career researchers in European security: research presentations, individualised feedback from senior scholars, and structured mentorship. Travel and hotel reimbursement is available for 15 PhD students, and selected participants receive free access to the European Security Conference that follows.

events.summary: NetSec Policy Workshop: Great Power Politics and the Future of Alliances
events.description:
A NetSec Working Group 2 policy workshop on great power politics and the future of alliances, convening scholars and policy practitioners to examine how alliance politics is evolving under intensifying great power competition, and what the implications are for European security.

Accommodation in Ankara and all meals are provided by Bilkent University and the Royal Danish Defence College. NetSec plans to reimburse accepted participants' travel costs through COST Action NetSec up to a maximum of €700 per participant, pending a decision by NetSec's Management Committee.

Applications closed on 15 August 2026. Applicants have been informed of the outcome, and invitations to take part in person have gone out. A link for online participation will be circulated ahead of the workshop. Full details: https://netsec-cost.eu/policy-workshop-2026.html

cardDescription.en: Working Group 2's one-day policy workshop on great power politics and the future of alliances, held at Bilkent University, Ankara, on 13 September 2026. Accommodation and meals were provided by Bilkent University and the Royal Danish Defence College.

L'hébergement et les repas ont été pris en charge par l'Université Bilkent et le Collège de défense royal danois.
cardDescription.de: Der eintägige Politik-Workshop der Arbeitsgruppe 2 zu Großmachtpolitik und der Zukunft der Bündnisse, am 13. September 2026 an der Bilkent-Universität in Ankara abgehalten. Unterkunft und Verpflegung wurden von der Bilkent-Universität und dem Royal Danish Defence College bereitgestellt.

events.description:
The Action's first formal Management Committee plenary, held online, bringing together the MC representatives from the participating COST Member countries to align on workstreams, confirm Working Group leadership for the coming cycle, and elect any remaining roles.

Access was restricted to MC representatives, Working Group leads, and invited observers.

cardDescription.en: The Action's first formal plenary meeting, bringing together Management Committee representatives and Working Group leads to align on workstreams, confirm leadership for the coming cycle, and elect any remaining roles. The Action officially started on 10 October 2025, and this was its first plenary.
cardDescription.fr: La première réunion plénière formelle de l'Action, rassemblant les représentant·es du Comité de gestion et les responsables des groupes de travail pour s'aligner sur les chantiers, confirmer les positions de direction pour le cycle à venir et élire les rôles restants. L'Action a officiellement débuté le 10 octobre 2025, et il s'agissait de sa première plénière.
cardDescription.de: Die erste formelle Plenarsitzung der Aktion, die die Vertreter·innen des Management-Ausschusses und die Arbeitsgruppen-Leitungen zusammenbrachte, um die Arbeitsstränge abzustimmen, die Leitung für den kommenden Zyklus zu bestätigen und verbleibende Rollen zu wählen. Die Aktion startete offiziell am 10. Oktober 2025, und dies war ihr erstes Plenum.
